source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Classify prisms and pyramids from their faces and count their faces, edges, and vertices in the n-sided case.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Edge is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Classify prisms and pyramids from their faces and count their faces' is answered as edge rather than face.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Solid name and face-edge-vertex structure is what produces face arrangement and base shape, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Classify prisms and pyramids from their faces and count.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: face is settled by running 'Construct and reason with perpendicular projections of points, lines': A point projects to a plane at the foot of a perpendicular from the point to the plane — on the item about Classify prisms and pyramids from their faces and count.

intelligence.enrichment: Faces are flat boundary surfaces, edges are line segments where faces meet, and vertices are points where edges meet; an n-gonal prism has n+2 faces, 3n edges, and 2n vertices, while an n-gonal pyramid has n+1 faces, 2n edges, and n+1 vertices.
